title: Harmonize retry shaper and stream partitioning for async workers
creator: Priya Kannan
description:
Problem: Over the last year we have accumulated multiple, slightly incompatible retry/backoff implementations across Redis Stream consumers and Kafka workers. Each service implements its own retry timing, jitter, and DLQ handling. This causes:
- inconsistent retry budgets and customer-visible delays when downstream is degraded,
- unexpected worker stalls during cascade retries,
- duplicated work across partitions when partitioning logic and retries race, and
- difficulty reasoning about end-to-end latency and cost for heavy workloads.

Goal: Replace the ad-hoc retry code with a small, well-instrumented 'retry-shaper' library and unify stream partitioner rules so workers behave consistently under backpressure. The ticket scopes:
1) Implement retry-shaper library (python) providing: fixed/exponential backoff, configurable jitter strategies, attempt accounting, DLQ handoff, and hooks for prefix/KV cache invalidation. Library must emit metrics (attempts, retries_by_reason, retry_latency_histogram).
2) Redis Streams: move retry handling from per-service timers to retry-shaper integrated with consumer lease logic. Introduce a retry-stream pattern (xadd to <stream>:retries with scheduled timestamp payload) and a lightweight reconcilier that moves entries back to processing stream when due.
3) Kafka: harmonize commit semantics: use cooperative rebalancing + at-least-once with retry-shaper to avoid processing duplicates on retry; update consumer group config and bump aiokafka to 2.8.0 for cooperative group support.
4) Provide feature-flagged rollout and canary config so we can enable library incrementally by queue/namespace.

Non-goals: full cross-language SDK (we'll provide a well-documented HTTP shim for non-Python consumers in a follow-up ticket).

Success metrics (targets for runtime-1.24):
- Reduce median downstream-induced stall time caused by retries by 60% for top 20 queues,
- Decrease duplicate processing (retries causing duplicate side effects) by 30% measured by idempotency key collisions,
- No increase in 99th percentile process-to-ack latency for healthy queues.
acceptance_criteria: retry-shaper library published to internal PyPI with semver and pinned in runtime image
Redis streams move to retry-stream pattern behind a feature flag and tests demonstrating scheduled replays
Kafka consumers updated to use cooperative rebalancing + retry-shaper and validated with integration test harness
Instrumentation: new prometheus metrics for retry attempts, per-queue retry backlog, and retry service latency visible in console
Canary rollout executed for 3 non-critical namespaces and monitored for 72h with no customer-impacting regressions
Migration doc + runbook describing fallback to old behavior and DLQ inspection steps

implementation_notes:
Key decisions: 1) Use centralized retry-shaper to simplify metrics and rollout; 2) For Redis, use a separate ':retries' stream and a reconciler to avoid long blocking sleeps in workers; 3) For Kafka, leverage cooperative rebalancing and at-least-once semantics with careful commit points to minimize duplicates.

Trade-offs: Moving retries out of per-worker in-process timers improves operational observability but increases write amplification (extra stream writes) and requires reconciler capacity. Chosen mitigation: bounded reconciler workers + backpressure on enqueue when retry backlog exceeds SLO-derived thresholds.

Planned dependency upgrades: redis-py -> 5.3.7 (for improved streams API), aiokafka -> 2.8.0, prometheus-client pinned to 0.16.0. Coordinate upgrades with infra-image team to avoid runtime regressions.
